scope: Mayfair 2010/2013 English 2–4-player base; previous-Mayfair unified base clarifications only. No expansions or optional Gamble Variant.

required_facts: Remove End of Game, shuffle, deal two property cards per player.
Mark those two lots; take starting money equal to the sum of their printed card money values, used only in setup.
Discard by color/Strip with counts visible.
Divide remaining shuffled deck into four roughly equal stacks; End of Game on top of fourth, other three on top.
answers.expected_answer: Remove End of Game, shuffle, deal two property cards per player. Mark those two lots; take starting money equal to the sum of their printed card money values, used only in setup. Discard by color/Strip with counts visible. Divide remaining shuffled deck into four roughly equal stacks; End of Game on top of fourth, other three on top.
answers.source_references: Original p2 Setting Up; unified p5

required_facts: Each rolls two dice; highest roller takes player card and first turn.
Pass player card left after each turn.
Draw property card, take its lot, pay all owned lots, pay/score indicated casinos, discard appropriately, then Play actions.
answers.expected_answer: Each rolls two dice; highest roller takes player card and first turn. Pass player card left after each turn. Draw property card, take its lot, pay all owned lots, pay/score indicated casinos, discard appropriately, then Play actions.
answers.source_references: Original p2 Taking Turns/On Every Turn; p3 Ending Step 1

required_facts: Place your marker before payouts.
All marked lots including newly acquired lot pay their owner $1.
Card money values are used only during setup, not drawn-turn income.
answers.expected_answer: Place your marker before payouts. All marked lots including newly acquired lot pay their owner $1. Card money values are used only during setup, not drawn-turn income.
answers.source_references: Original p2 Setting Up/Take Over Your Lot/Owned Lots Pay

required_facts: Tile stays; replace opposing die with your own retaining current value 5, not printed 2.
Acquisition precedes payouts, so you receive $5 for that die when its casino pays.
answers.expected_answer: Tile stays; replace opposing die with your own retaining current value 5, not printed 2. Acquisition precedes payouts, so you receive $5 for that die when its casino pays.
answers.source_references: Original p2 Take Over Your Lot/Money Paid

required_facts: Edge-connected same-color tiles on same block form a single indivisible casino; diagonal-only contact does not.
Boss is owner of highest individual die, not greatest total pips or most tiles.
Casino colors do not denote player colors.
answers.expected_answer: Edge-connected same-color tiles on same block form a single indivisible casino; diagonal-only contact does not. Boss is owner of highest individual die, not greatest total pips or most tiles. Casino colors do not denote player colors.
answers.source_references: Original p1 Casino Tiles/Player Dice; p2 Who Owns What

required_facts: Red receives $7: $5 die plus $2 lots.
Blue receives $5 from dice.
Red boss receives 3 casino points, Blue no casino points.
answers.expected_answer: Red receives $7: $5 die plus $2 lots. Blue receives $5 from dice. Red boss receives 3 casino points, Blue no casino points.
answers.source_references: Original p2 Owned Lots Pay/Money Paid/Points Earned

required_facts: Color pays all casinos of that color anywhere.
Strip pays all colors with at least one casino edge adjacent to Strip.
Entire qualifying casino pays money/points for all tiles, not only touching tile.
answers.expected_answer: Color pays all casinos of that color anywhere. Strip pays all colors with at least one casino edge adjacent to Strip. Entire qualifying casino pays money/points for all tiles, not only touching tile.
answers.source_references: Original p2 Pay Based on Color/Pay The Strip; unified p8

required_facts: Build, sprawl, remodel, reorganize, gamble in any order.
All may repeat except gamble once per own turn; reorganization also limited per die per turn.
No player takes actions on another player’s turn; trading may occur at any time.
answers.expected_answer: Build, sprawl, remodel, reorganize, gamble in any order. All may repeat except gamble once per own turn; reorganization also limited per die per turn. No player takes actions on another player’s turn; trading may occur at any time.
answers.source_references: Original p3 Step 2 Play/Reorganize; p4 Trading

required_facts: Pay $6; choose available casino tile color.
Remove/reclaim marker, place tile on your owned lot and your die set to board value 2.
Same-color edge neighbors merge automatically.
answers.expected_answer: Pay $6; choose available casino tile color. Remove/reclaim marker, place tile on your owned lot and your die set to board value 2. Same-color edge neighbors merge automatically.
answers.source_references: Original p3 Build; unified p10 Build

required_facts: Pay $18, place available gold tile with own die 3.
Must boss origin; target empty unowned and edge-adjacent; neither opponent-owned nor diagonal-only target is legal.
Cannot sprawl without available tile of same color.
answers.expected_answer: Pay $18, place available gold tile with own die 3. Must boss origin; target empty unowned and edge-adjacent; neither opponent-owned nor diagonal-only target is legal. Cannot sprawl without available tile of same color.
answers.source_references: Original p3 Sprawl

required_facts: Must boss casino; remodel all its tiles into one new color with enough available tiles.
Pay $10 ($5 each); replace all tiles with new-color tiles; dice/holdings remain.
Edge-adjacent same-color casinos merge; owner of larger die becomes boss even if another player.
answers.expected_answer: Must boss casino; remodel all its tiles into one new color with enough available tiles. Pay $10 ($5 each); replace all tiles with new-color tiles; dice/holdings remain. Edge-adjacent same-color casinos merge; owner of larger die becomes boss even if another player.
answers.source_references: Original p3 Remodel and example; unified p11

required_facts: Yes, at least one own die suffices; acting player pays $10 total pips of all dice.
All dice reroll, each owner rolling their own.
Each owner returns dice only to their own original tiles, choosing assignment among those tiles if multiple.
answers.expected_answer: Yes, at least one own die suffices; acting player pays $10 total pips of all dice. All dice reroll, each owner rolling their own. Each owner returns dice only to their own original tiles, choosing assignment among those tiles if multiple.
answers.source_references: Original p3 Reorganize

required_facts: No: no die may be reorganized more than once per turn, so any previously reorganized die prevents reorganization of the enlarged casino.
Boss-tie rerolls are free and not subject to reorganization once-per-turn limit.
answers.expected_answer: No: no die may be reorganized more than once per turn, so any previously reorganized die prevents reorganization of the enlarged casino. Boss-tie rerolls are free and not subject to reorganization once-per-turn limit.
answers.source_references: Original p3 Reorganize; p4 Reroll if Tied; unified p11

required_facts: Immediately reroll only tied largest dice at no cost.
If both become 3, Green unchanged 4 is boss; do not keep rerolling smaller 3s.
Same-player highest tie requires no reroll; ties below highest require none.
If different players remain tied for current highest, repeat with current highest until one player controls highest.
answers.expected_answer: Immediately reroll only tied largest dice at no cost. If both become 3, Green unchanged 4 is boss; do not keep rerolling smaller 3s. Same-player highest tie requires no reroll; ties below highest require none. If different players remain tied for current highest, repeat with current highest until one player controls highest.
answers.source_references: Original p4 After Each Action Reroll if Tied and diagram

required_facts: Maximum $15: minimum of $20 tile cap, own $18 and boss $15.
Give casino’s boss House card; must choose another player’s bossed casino.
Gamble once during own turn.
answers.expected_answer: Maximum $15: minimum of $20 tile cap, own $18 and boss $15. Give casino’s boss House card; must choose another player’s bossed casino. Gamble once during own turn.
answers.source_references: Original p4 Gamble

required_facts: 3/4/9/10/11: win $4 from boss and retain/get stake back.
2/12: nominal win $8 but receive only boss’s available $7 and retain/get stake back.
5/6/7/8: lose/pay $4 to boss.
answers.expected_answer: 3/4/9/10/11: win $4 from boss and retain/get stake back. 2/12: nominal win $8 but receive only boss’s available $7 and retain/get stake back. 5/6/7/8: lose/pay $4 to boss.
answers.source_references: Original p4 Gamble; unified p13

required_facts: Trade at any time even off-turn; money, lots, casino dice and actions on acting player’s current turn.
Replace lot marker with recipient marker; replace die with recipient die at same current pip value, not board value.
No points or casino tiles; no promises of future-turn actions/exchanges/transfers.
No actions on another player’s turn.
answers.expected_answer: Trade at any time even off-turn; money, lots, casino dice and actions on acting player’s current turn. Replace lot marker with recipient marker; replace die with recipient die at same current pip value, not board value. No points or casino tiles; no promises of future-turn actions/exchanges/transfers. No actions on another player’s turn.
answers.source_references: Original p4 Trading

required_facts: 1 leaves 8; 2 or 3 reaches 10; 4 or 5 reaches 12.
Insufficient excess at a break is lost; cannot pool separate casino awards.
Score each casino independently smallest to largest, player chooses equal-size order; two single-tile awards leave 8.
answers.expected_answer: 1 leaves 8; 2 or 3 reaches 10; 4 or 5 reaches 12. Insufficient excess at a break is lost; cannot pool separate casino awards. Score each casino independently smallest to largest, player chooses equal-size order; two single-tile awards leave 8.
answers.source_references: Original p2 Scoring; p3 scoring example and multiple casinos

required_facts: Game ends immediately; no subsequent Play actions.
Final payout all owned lots and casinos touching Strip, with ordinary money and scoring rules.
Most points wins; tied most points breaks by most money.
90+ points wins immediately in base game.
answers.expected_answer: Game ends immediately; no subsequent Play actions. Final payout all owned lots and casinos touching Strip, with ordinary money and scoring rules. Most points wins; tied most points breaks by most money. 90+ points wins immediately in base game.
answers.source_references: Original p4 Winning; unified p16

required_facts: No building on F block.
Setup F card is discarded and replaced; valid two cards determine initial properties/money.
During turn do not mark F; pay owned lots and indicated casinos/points, discard then repeat Draw until A–E card resolved.
Each such draw pays, so multiple payouts in one turn before Play; End of Game still ends immediately.
answers.expected_answer: No building on F block. Setup F card is discarded and replaced; valid two cards determine initial properties/money. During turn do not mark F; pay owned lots and indicated casinos/points, discard then repeat Draw until A–E card resolved. Each such draw pays, so multiple payouts in one turn before Play; End of Game still ends immediately.
answers.source_references: Original p4 2-Player Rules/Winning; unified p16 2-Player Rules

required_facts: The tenth is a replacement, not a tenth usable tile.
Cannot build gold, sprawl gold or remodel to gold without sufficient available tiles.
A different available color may be built on own lot at normal cost.
answers.expected_answer: The tenth is a replacement, not a tenth usable tile. Cannot build gold, sprawl gold or remodel to gold without sufficient available tiles. A different available color may be built on own lot at normal cost.
answers.source_references: Original p1 Casino Tiles; p3 Available Tiles/Build/Sprawl/Remodel

required_facts: Remove one of your existing ownership dice and place it on the new tile at the value required by the placement.
Vacated tile remains ownerless but counts for casino points.
If no dice remain in a casino it has no owner/boss.
Trading may free a die.
answers.expected_answer: Remove one of your existing ownership dice and place it on the new tile at the value required by the placement. Vacated tile remains ownerless but counts for casino points. If no dice remain in a casino it has no owner/boss. Trading may free a die.
answers.source_references: Original p3 Available Dice; unified p6 Available Dice

required_facts: Place own die at printed board value 2; former removed value 5 is not retained.
Tile remains; takeover precedes matching casino payout, which includes your $2 for that die.
answers.expected_answer: Place own die at printed board value 2; former removed value 5 is not retained. Tile remains; takeover precedes matching casino payout, which includes your $2 for that die.
answers.source_references: Original p2 Take Over Your Lot/Money Paid; unified p7

required_facts: Leave your existing die unchanged at 6.
Matching payout pays you $6 for that die.
answers.expected_answer: Leave your existing die unchanged at 6. Matching payout pays you $6 for that die.
answers.source_references: Unified p7 Step 2; original p2 Money Paid

required_facts: Move one existing marker to newly gained lot.
You no longer own vacated lot; it does not pay you lot income.
New marked lot pays you $1 in upcoming payout.
answers.expected_answer: Move one existing marker to newly gained lot. You no longer own vacated lot; it does not pay you lot income. New marked lot pays you $1 in upcoming payout.
answers.source_references: Unified p6 Available Player Markers; original p2 Draw/Owned Lots Pay

required_facts: Money, piece counts and discarded cards are public; anyone may inspect discards.
Bank money unlimited; physical bank exhaustion does not cancel a payout.
answers.expected_answer: Money, piece counts and discarded cards are public; anyone may inspect discards. Bank money unlimited; physical bank exhaustion does not cancel a payout.
answers.source_references: Original p1 Money; unified p6 Your Resources/Available Money

required_facts: Green’s replacement die retains value6.
The remaining Red6 and new Green6 are tied for highest across different players; reroll those two dice immediately, not Blue3 initially.
Finish resolving any current-highest cross-player ties before actions or initiating more trades; after each reroll reassess the current highest dice and stop when one player owns the highest value.

For physical roller identity, the supplied free boss-tie rules do not explicitly designate who throws each die. They specify which owners’ dice participate. The each-player-rolls-own instruction is expressly part of paid Reorganization, not a stated universal free-tie actor rule. Do not invent a mandatory owner-only allocation or an any-person permission.
answers.expected_answer: Green’s replacement die retains value6. The remaining Red6 and new Green6 are tied for highest across different players; reroll those two dice immediately, not Blue3 initially. Finish resolving any current-highest cross-player ties before actions or initiating more trades; after each reroll reassess the current highest dice and stop when one player owns the highest value. For physical roller identity, the supplied free boss-tie rules do not explicitly designate who throws each die. They specify which owners’ dice participate. The each-player-rolls-own instruction is expressly part of paid Reorganization, not a stated universal free-tie actor rule. Do not invent a mandatory owner-only allocation or an any-person permission.
answers.source_references: Original p4 Trading/Reroll if Tied and its narrative/example; unified physicalp9 Settling Who’s the Boss; originalp3/unifiedp11 Reorganize for the expressly local roller instruction.

Reroll only current highest dice free; this is not paid reorganization and does not use its limit.

required_facts: Sole owner may reorganize; no-own-die casino may not.
Reorganization always rerolls every die and costs all pips, including opponents, not just selected own dice.
answers.expected_answer: Sole owner may reorganize; no-own-die casino may not. Reorganization always rerolls every die and costs all pips, including opponents, not just selected own dice.

required_facts: Any dice may be used to gamble; no ownership placement or removal required for the gambling roll.
Cannot gamble at own casino; if no opponent bosses a casino there is no legal gambling action.

Cannot sprawl without boss control.
